summary: Inference-time optimization can reduce LLM API spend by 60-90% without retraining or sacrificing quality, primarily through prompt caching, semantic caching, and intelligent model routing. Production teams commonly cut monthly bills from $10K to $2K by combining a few techniques. The highest-leverage move is prompt caching, which alone can cut repeated-prompt input costs by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse cached results of repeated prefix tokens (system prompts, few-shot examples, long context) so the provider charges a steep discount on cached portions instead of re-processing them on every call.
techniques.example: Place your static 2,000-token system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI serves them from cache, charging ~10% of the normal input rate for that prefix.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store prior query/response pairs and serve a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (via embedding similarity) rather than requiring an exact string match, eliminating redundant LLM calls entirely.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache so that 'What's your refund policy?' and 'How do I get a refund?' both return the same stored answer without hitting the API.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, escalating to a more expensive model only when a small/cheap model's confidence or validation fails.
techniques.example: Send all queries to GPT-4o-mini first and only fall back to GPT-4o for the ~15% of cases where the mini model returns low confidence or fails a validation check.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Minimization
techniques.description: Trim redundant words, boilerplate, and verbose instructions, and compress long context using tools like LLMLingua to reduce the number of input tokens per call.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-word verbose system prompt with a tight 150-word version and run retrieved documents through LLMLingua before injecting them into context.

techniques.name: Output Token Capping
techniques.description: Set max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise or respond in structured/JSON format, since output tokens are often priced 3-5x higher than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=200 and add 'Respond in under 3 sentences' instead of letting the model ramble to its default limit.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) instead of large context
techniques.description: Retrieve only the most relevant chunks for a query rather than stuffing entire documents into the prompt, drastically reducing input tokens per call.
techniques.example: Instead of pasting a 50-page manual into every prompt, embed it once and retrieve only the 3 most relevant paragraphs per user question.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batch API call to benefit from batch pricing discounts and reduced per-request overhead.
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 non-urgent classification tasks through OpenAI's Batch API overnight to get ~50% off standard rates.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required answer or stop sequence is produced, avoiding paying for unneeded trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '</answer>' so generation halts the moment the structured answer is complete rather than continuing to a fixed limit.

techniques.name: Cost-per-Task Tracking & Observability
techniques.description: Measure total cost per completed task (including retries and failures), not just raw token counts, so a 'cheaper' model that needs retries doesn't quietly cost more.
techniques.example: Use Helicone or LangSmith to flag that a cheap model requires 2.5 retries on average, making it more expensive per successful task than a pricier single-shot model.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned / Distilled Small Models
techniques.description: Distill knowledge from a large model into a smaller one or use a fine-tuned small model for high-volume narrow tasks, cutting per-token cost and allowing shorter prompts.
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini on your support tickets so it handles triage without a long few-shot prompt, replacing expensive GPT-4o calls.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer for LLM queries that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to cut redundant API calls.

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store offering vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses to reduce token usage and latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK to call 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallback, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Enterprise tier custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing cost tracking, caching, and request logging per model and user.

tools.name: LangChain / LangSmith
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with caching integrations, plus LangSmith for tracing, evaluation, and cost-per-task monitoring.
tools.pricing_paid: LangChain free OSS; LangSmith free tier, paid from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that reduces prompt length while preserving meaning, lowering input token counts.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, routing, load balancing, fallbacks, and observability across providers.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API that routes requests across many model providers, enabling easy model cascading and price comparison.

tools.name: Martian / Model Router
tools.description: Dynamic model routing that sends each request to the best-cost/performance model automatically.

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by placing static system prompts and few-shot examples at the start of every request to cut input costs by up to 90%.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM to eliminate redundant calls for similar queries with ~68% hit rates.
Switch high-volume, simple tasks to a cheaper small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only escalate to a flagship model on failure.
Set max_tokens and instruct concise/structured output to reduce the expensive output-token bill by 20-40%.
Instrument cost-per-task tracking with Helicone or LiteLLM so you optimize true total cost rather than raw token counts.
